messages.content: Research mobile point-of-sale UX for a field sales app used ONE-HANDED on cheap Android phones in Indonesian shops. Be concrete, name real apps/patterns. 1) Which real mobile apps moved the search or address bar to the BOTTOM and what specifically did it fix? 2) For adding many line items fast, compare tap-to-increment directly on a list row vs a +/- stepper vs opening a quantity modal. Which wins when a basket is 15 lines of qty 1-3, and which wins for 3 lines of qty 200? 3) Bottom-sheet cart patterns in POS and food-ordering apps: what must the COLLAPSED state show so the user never opens it just to check? 4) Smallest reliable tap target and row height for a scrolling product list used one-handed while standing. 5) Common failure modes when a POS list uses tap-to-add without confirmation feedback. Terse, specific, no preamble, no disclaimers.
